summary: Georg Morgenstierne worked in Indology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and linguistics. He studied at Oslo, Bonn, and Humboldt University of Berlin (PhD) under Konow, Lüders, Jacobi, Beckh, and Schulze, holding professorships at Gothenburg (1930–1937) and Oslo (1937–1962).

Georg Renatus Solta was an Austrian linguist who earned his PhD at the University of Vienna (1934–1939) studying under Paul Kretschmer and Wilhelm Havers. He served at Vienna as Privatdozent from 1953 and associate professor of Indo-European linguistics from 1967.
Georg Simmel was a philosopher who studied at Humboldt University of Berlin from circa 1876 to 1881 and later taught there from circa 1885 to 1914.

Philosopher Georg Wilhelm Friedrich Hegel studied at the Tübinger Stift and University of Tübingen, as well as Jena. He taught at Jena, directed the Aegidianum Nürnberg, and served as professor at Heidelberg (~1816–1818) and Frederick William University Berlin (~1818–1831).

Georg von Simson is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Mainz and Göttingen (PhD) under Ernst Waldschmidt, worked at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities (1968–1977), and was professor at the University of Oslo (1977–2003).

Georg von der Gabelentz studied at Jena, Halle-Wittenberg under August Friedrich Pott, TU Dresden, and Leipzig (PhD). A specialist in Sinology, linguistics, and Japanology, he was professor at Leipzig (1878–1889) and Humboldt University of Berlin from 1889.

George A. Kennedy was a scholar of Sinology and linguistics who studied at Humboldt University of Berlin (circa 1932–1935) under Erich Haenisch and Otto Franke. He held an academic post at Yale University from circa 1935 to 1960.

George A. Keyworth specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He earned degrees at UC Santa Barbara and a PhD at UCLA under Robert E. Buswell Jr. He held professorships at the University of Colorado Boulder (2001) and University of Saskatchewan (2011).

George Abraham Grierson studied at Trinity College Dublin, Cambridge, and Halle-Wittenberg (PhD). Active in linguistics and Indology, he served in the Indian Civil Service, directed the Linguistic Survey of India (1898–1928), and was director of SOAS (1917–1925).

George Adolphus Jacob was an Indologist educated at Sheffield Collegiate School. He served in the Bombay Staff Corps and Indian Army, was Acting Superintendent at Native Army School, Poona (1862–1865), and became a fellow of the University of Mumbai (attested 1894).

George Baumann is an Indologist who earned his PhD at Heidelberg University (circa 1968–1973) and studied at Bibliothekar-Lehrinstitut Nordrhein-Westfalen. He worked at the University of Tübingen and served as Bibliotheksreferendar at Tübingen University Library from 1976 to 2001.

George Bidie worked in Indology and history/archaeology. He studied at Marischal College, Aberdeen (MD 1849–1853) and Edinburgh. He served as professor of botany at Madras Medical College (1866–1870) and superintendent of the Government Museum, Chennai (1872–1884).
George Bogle was an 18th-century figure in Tibetology and history/archaeology who studied at Enfield Academy and the University of Edinburgh.

George Bosworth Burch worked in philosophy and Indology, studying at Harvard (AB), Geneva, and Paris. He was professor of philosophy and psychology at the College of Idaho (1942–1946) and Fletcher Professor of Philosophy at Tufts University (1946–1967).
George Byres Mainwaring was a scholar of linguistics and Indology who served as an ensign in the Bengal Army (1842) and reached the rank of lieutenant-colonel in the Bengal Staff Corps (1868).

George C. O. Haas was an Indologist who earned his AB and PhD at Columbia University under A. V. Williams Jackson. He taught German at City College of New York (1904–1916) and served as editor for the Journal of the American Oriental Society.
George Campbell was a scholar of Indology and linguistics who studied at the University of St Andrews, East India Company College, and the University of Oxford, where he received a D.C.L. in 1874.

George Cardona was an Indologist and linguist. He studied at NYU and Yale, completing his PhD under Warren Crawford Cowgill and Paul Thieme. He spent his career as a professor of linguistics at the University of Pennsylvania from circa 1965 to 2007.
George Carstairs was a scholar of religious studies and Indology who received his education at The Albany Academy and the University of Glasgow, earning an M.A. (circa 1897–1901) and a D.D. (1935).

George Chatalian was a philosopher and scholar of Buddhist studies who earned his A.B. at Brown University and his Ph.D. at Harvard University (~1958–1968). He held teaching posts at Franklin Pierce University, Obafemi Awolowo University (1983), and the University of Lagos.
